newsitem.title: USA: Hilton files final proxy in ITT bid.
newsitem.headline: Hilton files final proxy in ITT bid.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp. filed its final proxy solicitation with regulators on Friday, clearing the way for the company to seek shareholder votes in its attempt to unseat ITT Corp.'s board of directors.

Hilton, in an aggressive move to put its $6.5 billion bid for ITT to a shareholder vote, also has been asking ITT's largest stockholders to sign an affidavit supporting their legal motion for a mid-May annual meeting.
"The message there is (ITT shareholders) are fully capable of making a decision" by mid-May, said Marc Grossman, senior vice president of corporate affairs at Hilton.

Hilton launched its hostile bid for ITT, owner of Sheraton Hotels, Caesars World Casinos and a host of entertainment assets, in January. ITT promptly rejected the bid and has embarked on a strategy of selling non-core assets, including a $650 million deal to sell Madison Square Garden Inc.

In federal court in Las Vegas, Hilton has asked U.S. District Judge Philip Pro to force ITT into holding an annual meeting around its traditional time in mid-May. At the meeting, Hilton will attempt to unseat ITT's board.

As a rebuttal, ITT has filed a counterclaim to Hilton's motion saying, among other things, it needs time to allow its new strategy to take hold before shareholders can decide who is more fit to run ITT, current management or Hilton.
Grossman said Hilton would begin mailing the proxies to ITT shareholders next week.

Separately, Hilton acknowledged it sent a letter to Atlantic City officials inquiring about possibly purchasing a piece of land that rival gaming firm Mirage Resorts Inc. has been trying to develop for about two years.

The land, commonly called the "H-Tract," is near Atlantic City's marina district. Mirage, Circus Circus Enterprises Inc. ( ) and Boyd Gaming Corp. all have plans to develop Las Vegas-style resort casinos in the district.

But Mirage, which has a contract with the city to develop the land, has been opposed by Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc. Chairman Donald Trump, who is arguing against city subsidies for a highway and tunnel to the tract.

Mirage was nearing a May 5 deadline to complete work that would have enabled it to receive certain permits to continue to develop the land, and was about to ask for an extension of that date, said Arthur Goldberg, president of Hilton's gaming division.
"They couldn't reach those dates before the contract was open to being renegotiated, and that was the only reason we participated" by sending the letter, Goldberg told Reuters.
But Mirage had a decidedly different point of view.
In a statement, Mirage said Hilton's move "is a blatantly improper attempt to interfere with our contract" and it "has no intention of abandoning (the) project."
Goldberg said Hilton has received expressions of interest from some city council members, but he declined to name them. He said Hilton would have meetings with several of council members next week.

He said a Hilton project would likely abandon the tunnel, and most importantly, not seek a subsidy to build the highway. Goldberg said Hilton could have an outline within 90 days and begin construction within four to five months.
